examples.en: On Memorial Day I visited the national cemetery.
The national cemetery is a quiet and solemn place.
Many people visit the national cemetery every year.
We went on a school field trip to the national cemetery.
I took off my hat in front of the national cemetery.
The national cemetery is not far from my house.

explain: 나라를 위해 일한 분들을 모신 곳이에요. '현충원'이라는 이름으로도 많이 불러요. 장소 이름이라 조용히 하고 예의를 지켜야 해요.

phrases.en: I visited the national cemetery with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가다'보다 일부러 방문한다는 느낌이 있어서 이런 장소에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more like a deliberate visit than 'go', which suits a place like this.

phrases.en: You have to be quiet at the national cemetery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 지킬 예의를 말할 때 '에서는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '에서는' when talking about manners to keep in that place.

phrases.en: I laid flowers at the national cemetery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국립묘지'를 다르게 부르는 이름이에요. 이름이 붙은 곳을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the national cemetery, often used for the named sites.

explain_en: It is a place that honors people who served the nation. It is also commonly called '현충원'. Since it is a solemn site, visitors should be quiet and respectful.

examples.en: Our house is next to the school.
Which countries neighbor Korea?
I live in a neighborhood next to the market.
The two cities are adjacent, so they are close.

examples.ko: 두 학교가 이웃했을 때는 같이 행사를 했어요.
examples.en: When the two schools were next to each other, they held events together.
If an apartment is next to a park, the air is good.

explain: '이웃하다'는 '~와/과 이웃하다'나 '이웃한 ~'처럼 두 곳이 가깝게 붙어 있을 때 써요. 사람이 옆집에 산다고 말할 때는 '이웃에 살다'나 '옆집에 살다'가 더 자연스러워요. 'ㅎ' 때문에 [이우타다]로 소리 나요.

phrases.en: I live in a city next to Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 옆에 붙어 있는 곳을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a place right next to another.

phrases.en: The two countries neighbor each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 곳이 가까이 붙어 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say two places are right beside each other.

phrases.en: These two cities are not next to each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있지 않을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for places that aren't adjacent.

explain_en: 이웃하다 is used in forms like '~와/과 이웃하다' or '이웃한 ~' when two places lie close together. For a person living next door, 이웃에 살다 or 옆집에 살다 sounds more natural. Because of ㅎ, it is pronounced [이우타다].

en: to be located; to be situated

examples.en: A small pond sits in the middle of the park.
An old church stood on top of the hill.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 큰 나무가 자리한 모습이 예뻐요.
examples.en: The sight of the big tree at the village entrance is pretty.
That cafe is at the end of the alley.

examples.ko: 강 옆에 자리한 집에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to live in a house by the river.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 시장 안쪽에 자리하고 있어서 찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: That restaurant is deep inside the market, so it is hard to find.

explain: '위치하다'와 거의 같고, '있다'보다 글이나 안내문 같은 느낌이에요. 여행 소개, 뉴스에서 '~에 자리한 ~'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 나와요. 주어는 보통 건물, 가게, 장소예요.

phrases.example: 그때 들은 말이 아직도 제 마음속에 자리하고 있어요.
phrases.en: stay in one's heart
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소가 아니라 기억이나 감정이 마음에 남아 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 글이나 노래 가사에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not for a place but for a memory or feeling that stays inside you. Common in writing and song lyrics.
phrases.en_equiv: to live on in one's heart

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '위치하다' and sounds more like writing or signage than plain '있다'. It often appears in travel guides and news in the modifying form '~에 자리한 ~' (the ~ located at ~). The subject is usually a building, shop or place.

dis.h: sit or stand in a place; descriptive

p.n: 소재하다 is more formal and sounds like an official document.

examples.en: Lots of cars pass along this road.

examples.ko: 아침마다 이 골목을 지나다니는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people pass through this alley every morning.

examples.ko: 매일 그 가게 앞을 지나다녔는데 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I passed by that shop every day but never noticed it.

examples.ko: 버스가 자주 지나다니는 길이라서 좀 시끄러워요.
examples.en: It is a road buses often pass along, so it is a bit noisy.
Drive slowly where children walk by.
I heard that long ago cows used to pass along this road.

explain: '지나가다'는 한 번 지나가는 것이고, '지나다니다'는 같은 곳을 자주 오가는 느낌이에요. '길을 지나다니다'나 '이 길로 지나다니다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: There are many people passing by in front of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지나다니다'를 사람을 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb turned into a modifier describing people.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 이 길을 매일 지나다녔어요.
phrases.en: When I was young, I passed along this road every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 자주 오간 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something you did often in the past.

phrases.example: 공사 중이니까 이 길로 지나다니지 마세요.
phrases.en: There is construction, so please don't walk along this road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳을 오가지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask someone not to go back and forth there.

explain_en: '지나가다' is passing once, while '지나다니다' means going back and forth past the same place often. You can say '길을 지나다니다' or '이 길로 지나다니다'.

examples.en: At low tide I picked up shells at the beachside.

examples.ko: 저녁 바람을 맞으며 해변가를 따라 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly along the beachside in the evening breeze.

examples.ko: 이 동네 해변가에 예쁜 카페가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many pretty cafés along the beach in this town.
In summer the children play happily at the beachside.
For this vacation I booked a place to stay by the beach.
I watched the sun rise at the beachside.

explain: '해변'만 써도 같은 곳을 말해요. '해변'에 '가'가 또 붙어 뜻이 겹치지만 말할 때는 자주 써요. 바닷가는 '바닷가에서 살다'처럼 사는 곳에도 쓰고, 해변은 놀러 가는 모래사장 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I took photos on the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해변가'와 거의 같고 더 짧게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 해변가 but shorter and more common.

phrases.en: There is a small house by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀러 가는 곳뿐 아니라 사는 곳도 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can refer to a place where you live, not only a place to visit.

phrases.en: I drink coffee at a beachside cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다 옆에 있는 가게를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a shop located next to the sea.

explain_en: Just '해변' can refer to the same place. 해변가 adds '가' (edge) to 해변, so the meaning overlaps, but people say it a lot in speech. '바닷가' also works for where people live ('바닷가에서 살다'), while 해변 feels more like a sandy beach for leisure.

examples.en: My grandfather collects old records.
I like the warm sound of records.
Dust has piled up on the record.
I saw a record spinning for the first time.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 레코드는 이제 구하기 어려워요.
examples.en: That singer's records are hard to find now.
I played music for my friend on a record.

explain: '레코드판'이라고도 하고 'LP'라고 부르기도 해요. 인터넷으로 듣는 음악은 '음원'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: An old song is coming out of the record.
phrases.nuance_ko: '레코드'보다 동그란 판 자체를 또렷하게 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clearer way to refer to the round disc itself.

phrases.en: My father played a record for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악을 재생한다는 뜻으로 '틀다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 틀다 to mean playing music.

phrases.en: I listen to music on LPs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 레코드판을 부르는 또 다른 말이에요. 말할 때는 '엘피'라고 읽어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the large record. When speaking, it is read aloud as 엘피 (el-pi).

explain_en: It is also called 'rekodeupan' or 'LP'. Music you listen to online is called 'eumwon'.

examples.en: I sketch trees in the park.
Yesterday I sketched the sea.
It rained while I was sketching.
A pencil is handy when you sketch.
I want to sketch my friend's face.
After sketching, I will add color.

explain: '그림을 그리다'보다 가볍게 대강 그린다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '풍경을 스케치하다'처럼 그리는 대상을 목적어로 써요.

phrases.example: 그림을 그리기 전에 먼저 연필로 스케치해 보세요.
phrases.en: Before drawing, try sketching with a pencil first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 권할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A suggestion form used when recommending that someone try sketching.

phrases.en: I sketch in the park every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스케치하다'와 뜻이 같고, 명사 '스케치'에 '를 하다'를 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword, built from the noun 'sketch' plus 'do'.

phrases.en: I went on a trip and sketched the sea view.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그리는 대상이 풍경일 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, when the thing being sketched is a landscape.

explain_en: It feels lighter than 'geurimeul geurida': a quick, rough drawing. The thing you draw is usually the object, as in 'punggyeongeul seukechihada'.

examples.en: The new movie's trailer came out today.
The trailer is only two minutes long.
I watched the trailer together with a friend.
My favorite actor appears in the trailer.
Even the trailer is fun, so I look forward to the movie.
The music in the trailer was really cool.

explain: 드라마의 다음 회 안내는 '다음 회 예고'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 영화에는 '예고편'을 써요. 둘 다 짧은 영상이에요.

phrases.en: I bought a ticket after watching the movie trailer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영화'를 앞에 붙여 무엇의 예고편인지 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 영화 makes clear what the trailer is for.

phrases.en: I'm watching a trailer before bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예고편을 볼 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for watching a trailer.

phrases.example: 드라마가 끝나고 다음 회 예고가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: After the drama ended, the next-episode preview came on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마의 다음 이야기를 알려 주는 짧은 영상에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the short preview of a drama's next episode.

explain_en: For a drama's next episode people often say '다음 회 예고', while '예고편' is used for movies. Both are short videos.

examples.en: The theme song of this movie is so good.
When I hear the theme song, I think of that drama.
Who sang the Olympic theme song?
I memorized the theme song lyrics and sang along.
My friend changed the ringtone to a cartoon's theme song.

examples.ko: 드라마 주제곡의 첫 소절만 들어도 알아요.
examples.en: I can tell from just the first line of the drama's theme song.

explain: '주제가'는 가사가 있는 노래를 가리키고, '주제곡'은 가사 없는 연주곡까지 넓게 가리킬 수 있어요. 영화, 드라마, 만화, 게임처럼 작품마다 대표 음악이 있을 때 써요.

phrases.en: I listen to this movie's theme song every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 작품 종류를 붙이면 어떤 작품의 주제곡인지 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the type of work in front makes clear which work the song belongs to.

phrases.en: My friend sang the drama's theme song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가사가 있는 주제곡을 노래할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sings a theme song that has lyrics.

phrases.en: The theme song came on at the end, and I cried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 드라마에서 음악이 흘러나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the music plays in a movie or drama.

explain_en: 주제가 points to a song with lyrics, while 주제곡 can also cover instrumental pieces without lyrics. You use it when a work such as a movie, drama, cartoon or game has a signature piece of music.

examples.en: The kids are playing in the dirt at the park.
My clothes got all dirty from playing in the dirt.
When I was little, I played in the dirt every day.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 흙장난이 세상에서 제일 재미있대요.
examples.en: My son says playing in the dirt is the most fun thing in the world.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에는 흙장난하기 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: After the rain, it's perfect for playing in the dirt.

examples.ko: 흙장난은 그만하고 손 씻고 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Stop playing in the dirt, wash your hands and eat.

explain: '흙장난하다'라고도 하고, 주로 어린아이의 놀이를 말해요. 비슷한 '모래놀이'는 모래로, 흙장난은 흙으로 노는 것이에요.

phrases.en: The child is playing with dirt in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흙장난을 하다'를 붙여 쓴 동사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, written as one word instead of '흙장난을 하다'.

phrases.en: My younger sibling likes playing with dirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이의 취향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a child's likes.
phrases.en_equiv: to like playing in the dirt

phrases.en: The children are playing in the sand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흙 대신 모래로 하는 비슷한 놀이예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar play, but with sand instead of dirt.

explain_en: You can also say '흙장난하다', and it mostly refers to young children's play. The similar '모래놀이' is playing with sand, while 흙장난 is playing with soil.

examples.ko: 조용한 가을밤에는 귀뚜라미 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: On a quiet autumn night, you can hear crickets loudly.
As the autumn night deepens, it gets colder and colder.
I spent the cool autumn night talking with a friend.

examples.ko: 가을밤엔 따뜻한 차 한 잔이 생각나요.
examples.en: On autumn nights, I think of a cup of warm tea.
An autumn night with a bright moon is good for a walk.
Please play music as quiet as an autumn night.

explain: 서늘하고 차분한 분위기가 먼저 떠올라서 달, 벌레 소리, 산책 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 같은 식으로 '여름밤, 겨울밤'도 써요. 가을의 하루를 말하는 '가을날'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: On a deep autumn night, I read a book alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤이 늦었다는 느낌을 더해 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feeling that the night is late.

phrases.en: After dinner, I took an evening walk on an autumn night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차분한 분위기와 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that suits the calm mood.

phrases.en: There are many stars in the autumn night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달이나 별 이야기를 할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the moon or stars.

explain_en: It brings to mind a cool, calm atmosphere, so it goes well with words like moon, insect sounds and walks. You can say '여름밤' and '겨울밤' in the same way. It is handy to remember it as a pair with '가을날', which refers to an autumn day.

examples.en: This restaurant was made by remodeling a house.

examples.ko: 골목 안에 있는 가정집에서 하숙을 해요.
examples.en: I lodge at a private house in the alley.
Since it's a private house, it's quieter than an office.
This shop looks like an ordinary house.
Please keep a fire extinguisher even in an ordinary home.

examples.ko: 옛 가정집을 카페로 바꾼 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many places where an old house was turned into a cafe.

explain: 가게, 사무실, 학교 같은 건물과 구분해서 사람이 사는 집을 말할 때 써요. '일반 가정집', '가정집을 개조하다'처럼 자주 나와요. 그냥 '집'이라고 해도 되지만 건물의 용도를 강조할 때 '가정집'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: There are many ordinary homes on this street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 회사가 아닌 보통 사람이 사는 집을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for ordinary houses where people live, not shops or offices.

phrases.en: They fixed up a house and opened a café.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 가게 같은 다른 용도로 바꿀 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a house is turned into something else, like a shop.

phrases.en: It's a restaurant with a homey feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게가 집처럼 편안한 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a shop feels cozy like a home.

explain_en: You use it to talk about a house where people live, as opposed to a shop, office or school. It appears in phrases like '일반 가정집' and '가정집을 개조하다'. You can just say '집', but '가정집' stresses the building's use.

examples.ko: 감나무 가지에 까치 한 쌍이 둥지를 틀었어요.
examples.en: A pair of magpies built a nest on the persimmon tree branch.

examples.ko: 담 너머 이웃집 감나무에서 감이 익어 가요.
examples.en: The persimmons are ripening on the neighbor's tree over the wall.

examples.ko: 우리 집 감나무에 감이 많이 열렸어요.
examples.en: Our persimmon tree has a lot of fruit.

examples.ko: 우리 집 감나무가 유독 크고 감도 커요.
examples.en: Our persimmon tree is especially big, and the persimmons are big too.

examples.ko: 가을이면 감나무에 주황색 감이 주렁주렁 달려요.
examples.en: In autumn, orange persimmons hang in clusters from the tree.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 마당에는 오래된 감나무가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old persimmon tree in my grandmother's yard.

explain: '감'은 열매이고 '감나무'는 그 열매가 열리는 나무예요. '감이 열리다', '감이 익다'와 함께 써요. 시골 마당이나 담장 풍경을 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: I rested for a while under the persimmon tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무 아래 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the place under the tree.

phrases.en: In autumn, persimmons grow on the persimmon tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무와 열매를 함께 말할 때 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence linking the tree and its fruit.

phrases.en: There is one persimmon tree in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무는 '그루'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Trees are counted with 그루.

explain_en: '감' is the fruit and '감나무' is the tree it grows on. It is used with '감이 열리다' (fruit grows) and '감이 익다' (fruit ripens). It comes up when describing a country yard or a fence scene.

examples.en: The company trains new employees for three months.

examples.ko: 부모는 아이를 바르게 교육시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: Parents want to bring their child up properly.

examples.ko: 학교는 모든 학생을 안전하게 지내도록 교육시켰어요.
examples.en: The school educated all the students to stay safe.
This center plans to train foreigners.

examples.ko: 새 요리사를 교육시키려면 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Training a new cook takes a long time.
Educating children is not easy.

explain: '교육하다'는 가르치는 일 자체이고, '교육시키다'는 누군가를 교육받게 하는 것이에요. 회사 연수나 공식적인 글에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '가르치다'가 훨씬 흔해요. 동물에게는 '훈련시키다'가 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: The teacher teaches the children Hangul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서는 '교육시키다'보다 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but much more common in everyday speech than '교육시키다'.

phrases.en: The company is training its new employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금 교육하는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' means the training is happening right now.

phrases.example: 다음 주부터 새 직원을 교육시킬 거예요.
phrases.en: I will train the new employee starting next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 일을 말할 때 쓰는 미래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future form for talking about what you will do.

explain_en: '교육하다' is the act of teaching; '교육시키다' is making someone receive education. It appears in company training and formal writing, while everyday speech uses '가르치다' far more. For animals, '훈련시키다' fits better.

p.n: 교육하다 is a plain 'educate'; 교육시키다 stresses the causing of training.
